title_en: Cao Xiaodong v. Yunnan Xiaguan Tuo Tea Co., Ltd. — dispute over trademark infringement
ruling_gist_en: The right to a registered trademark is an identifying civil right. The trademark owner not only has the right to prohibit others from using the registered trademark on identical or similar goods, but also has the right to use the registered trademark to identify its own goods or services, and to establish in the relevant public the connection between the trademark and the source of its goods. Whether the relevant public will be confused or mistaken includes both mistaking goods bearing the allegedly infringing mark for the trademark owner's goods or as having some connection with the trademark owner, and also mistaking the trademark owner's goods for the infringer's goods or misperceiving a connection between the trademark owner and the alleged infringer, thereby impeding the trademark owner's exercise of its exclusive right to use the registered trademark, and further substantially hindering the registered trademark from performing its identifying function.

full_text_en:
Cao Xiaodong v. Yunnan Xiaguan Tuocha Co., Ltd.

Dispute over Infringement of Trademark Rights

Ruling Summary

The right to a registered trademark is a civil right of identification. The trademark owner has the right not only to prohibit others from using the identical or similar registered trademark on the same or similar goods, but also has the right to use the registered trademark to identify its goods or services, establishing a connection between the trademark and the source of its goods in the minds of the relevant public. Whether the relevant public will be confused or mistaken includes not only mistaking the goods bearing the allegedly infringing mark as the goods of the trademark owner or as having some connection with the trademark owner, but also mistaking the goods of the trademark owner as the goods of the alleged infringer or mistaking that there is some connection between the trademark owner and the alleged infringer, thereby hindering the trademark owner from exercising its exclusive right to use the registered trademark and substantially impeding the registered trademark from fulfilling its identifying function.

Civil Judgment of the Supreme People's Court

(2017) Zui Gao Fa Min Zai No. 273

Re-Petitioner (Plaintiff at First Instance, Appellee at Second Instance): Cao Xiaodong.

Agent ad litem: Wang Jingbo, lawyer of Yunnan Fangzhong Law Firm.

Respondent (Defendant at First Instance, Appellant at Second Instance): Yunnan Xiaguan Tuocha (Group) Co., Ltd. Domicile: No. 13 West Jianshe Road, Xiaguan Town, Dali City, Yunnan Province.

Legal Representative: Chu Jiuyun, General Manager of the Company.

Agent ad litem: Chen Yi, lawyer of Yunnan Guantang Law Firm.

The re-petitioner, Cao Xiaodong, filed a petition for retrial with this Court, dissatisfied with the civil judgment (2016) Yun Min Zhong No. 738 rendered by the Yunnan High People's Court in the case of dispute over infringement of trademark rights against the respondent, Yunnan Xiaguan Tuocha (Group) Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Xiaguan Tuocha Company). This Court, by civil ruling (2017) Zui Gao Fa Min Shen No. 2069 dated June 28, 2017, ordered a retrial of this case. This Court formed a collegial panel in accordance with the law to hear this case. The trial of this case is now concluded.

Cao Xiaodong stated in his petition for retrial: First, the respondent used the four large characters "Jin Ge Tie Ma" (Golden Spear and Iron Horse) on its tea cakes, both on the outer packaging box and inside the box. The font was bold and black, and the characters were placed in prominent positions, arranged vertically. Although the "Jin Ge Tie Ma" registered by the re-petitioner is in traditional Chinese characters arranged horizontally, while the respondent used simplified Chinese characters, according to Chinese cultural traditions, there is no difference in the understanding of their meaning, especially when used on the packaging of the same goods, the general public would sufficiently consider it as the trademark name of the goods. The second-instance court's conclusion that the public could distinguish between them is clearly erroneous. Second, the second-instance court considered that, from the overall packaging and decoration of the allegedly infringing goods, the four characters "Jin Ge Tie Ma" were enlarged and prominent, also significant in the decoration. However, this mark was only used on the front of the packaging. The sides and back of the outer packaging clearly indicated the company name and address of Xiaguan Tuocha Company, and the upper left corner of the front bore Xiaguan Tuocha Company's own "Xiaguan Tuocha" trademark in prominent red. Therefore, as a whole, the relevant public would not mistake the allegedly infringing goods for the goods bearing the trademark in question or as having a specific connection with such goods. The re-petitioner contends that the second-instance court ignored the general judgment ability and thinking habits of the public. Using the prominent mark "Jin Ge Tie Ma" in a conspicuous position on the front of the goods' packaging is sufficient to make the public believe that the goods are closely related to the "Jin Ge Tie Ma" trademark, or even that "Jin Ge Tie Ma" is the trademark for such goods. Furthermore, the infringing goods sold by the respondent are available as full boxes or individual cakes. In particular, the four large characters "Jin Ge Tie Ma" are even more conspicuous and prominent on the packaging of individual cakes. Entering the six characters "Jin Ge Tie Ma Cha Ye" (Golden Spear and Iron Horse Tea) on any official website on the internet will display the infringing tea cakes sold by the respondent. The second-instance court only examined the outer packaging boxes of the infringing products sold by the respondent, without examining whether the packaging of the tea cakes inside the boxes constituted infringement. This leads to an incomplete and insufficient factual basis. Although the respondent marked the "Xiaguan Tuocha" trademark and the company address on its sold goods, these were not in conspicuous positions and were relatively small in size; the general public would not pay sufficient attention to them. The production of goods by whom and the use of a trademark are two different legal relationships and are not a statutory reason for the respondent's exemption from liability. According to Article 76 of the Trademark Law, using a mark identical or similar to another person's registered trademark as the name or decoration of goods on the same or similar goods, thereby misleading the public, constitutes an act infringing the exclusive right to use a registered trademark as provided in Article 57, Item (2) of the Trademark Law. Third, the second-instance court's use of the degree of trademark fame to measure the extent of legal protection violates the principle of equality before the law. A trademark is an identifier for distinguishing goods and is also the identification of goods, protected by law. The "Jin Ge Tie Ma" trademark legally registered by the re-petitioner is equally protected by law upon registration. The law does not interfere with or prohibit its use in literary works and daily life. The re-petitioner has lawfully used its registered trademark on goods. Any person or enterprise must comply with the Trademark Law and other laws and regulations. Whether intentional or negligent, once objective infringement occurs, the infringing party shall bear liability for infringement in accordance with the law. There is no necessary causal relationship between this and the degree of fame of the registered trademark. In summary, the second-instance court made erroneous findings. The re-petitioner requests this Court to correct them in accordance with the law.

Xiaguan Tuocha Company argued in its defense: First, regarding the respondent's use of "Jin Ge Tie Ma," it did not use these four characters alone but in conjunction with the characters "Jia Wu" and "Tie Bing" (iron cake) as "Jia Wu Jin Ge Tie Ma Tie Bing." Moreover, "Jin Ge Tie Ma" is a Chinese idiom that is not original or distinctive. Such a registered trademark cannot preclude others from using the mark. Second, the Yunnan High Court's judgment also stated that although there is phonetic and semantic similarity, the trademark is a combination of text and graphics. When printed on the goods' packaging, for the relevant public, the differences in visual effect are more impactful and can offset the confusion that might be caused by identical pronunciation and meaning. From the perspective of the relevant public, the goods of the petitioner and the respondent can be distinguished at a glance and would not be confused. Third, the respondent owns its own registered trademarks, "Xiaguan Tuocha" and "Song He Yan Nian" (Pine and Crane Longevity). These trademarks of the respondent are prominently displayed on the respondent's goods. This includes "Xiaguan Tuocha," which has a prominent red mark, and the product address of Xiaguan Tuocha Company. Additionally, the respondent's trademark "Xiaguan Tuocha" is a Chinese time-honored brand and a well-known trademark. The "Song He Yan Nian" trademark is a famous trademark in Yunnan Province. The petitioner's "Jin Ge Tie Ma" trademark, aside from its registration certificate, does not have recognition certified by any other national authority. In other words, the respondent's goods have no need to free-ride on the trademark in question to enhance their own recognition. Furthermore, "Jin Ge Tie Ma" is very common in literary works. Even if the relevant public notices these four characters, they would not connect the two, let alone mistakenly believe that both goods are produced by Cao Xiaodong or authorized by Cao Xiaodong. In summary, the two trademarks are neither identical nor similar, and they certainly would not mislead the public.

Cao Xiaodong filed a lawsuit with the court of first instance, requesting: 1. The defendant immediately cease the infringement of the plaintiff's exclusive right to use the registered trademark "Jin Ge Tie Ma" in Class 30 under Registration No. 5492697, and cease the sale of all infringing products bearing the characters "Jin Ge Tie Ma"; 2. The defendant publish a statement of apology and eliminate the adverse effects in provincial media (newspaper or radio station); 3. The defendant compensate the plaintiff for losses in the amount of RMB 1,260,000; 4. The defendant compensate the plaintiff for attorney's fees and other reasonable expenses totaling RMB 63,990; 5. The defendant bear the litigation costs of this case. The court of first instance found the following facts: On June 14, 2009, the plaintiff, Cao Xiaodong, registered and obtained Registered Trademark No. 5492697. This trademark is a combined mark of text and graphics. The text "Jin Ge Tie Ma" is in horizontal traditional Chinese characters, with a leaf pattern below the text "Jin Ge Tie Ma." The designated goods for this trademark are in Class 30: tea; honey; sugar; coffee; cereal preparations; flour preparations; pastries; seasonings; puffed fruit chips, vegetable chips; edible starch products (up to). The registration period is valid from June 14, 2009, to June 13, 2019. The defendant, Xiaguan Tuocha Company, registered and obtained Registered Trademarks No. 6209882 and No. 12201774 on January 21, 2010, and September 7, 2014, respectively. These two trademarks are a combined mark consisting of the text "Song He Yan Nian" + a circle + a crane pattern, and a word mark "Xiaguan Tuocha," respectively. The designated goods for both trademarks include tea among other Class 30 goods. In 2014 (the Year of the Horse according to the lunar calendar), the defendant used the characters "Jia Wu Jin Ge Tie Ma Tie Bing" on the packaging of its Jin Yin series products, in simplified Chinese characters. Among these, the characters "Jia Wu" and "Tie Bing" were smaller in font, while the four characters "Jin Ge Tie Ma" were larger in font and located in conspicuous positions on both the outer and inner packaging of the tea cakes. Next to the four characters "Jin Ge Tie Ma" was a pattern of a horse in a galloping posture. Additionally, the defendant marked the registered trademark "Song He Yan Nian" and the characters "Xiaguan Tuocha" on both the inner and outer packaging of the said tea cakes, and also indicated the defendant's company name, Xiaguan Tuocha Company, on the inner and outer packaging. In February 2015, the plaintiff's agent ad litem, Wang Jingbo, sent a "Lawyer's Letter" to the defendant, stating that the defendant's production and sale of "Jia Wu·Jin Ge Tie Ma·Tie Bing" infringed the plaintiff's exclusive right to use the "Jin Ge Tie Ma" trademark, demanding that the defendant immediately cease the infringement, compensate for losses, and make an apology. The plaintiff alleged that the defendant's use of the "Jin Ge Tie Ma" mark on its produced and sold products infringed the plaintiff's exclusive right to use the registered trademark, and thus filed the lawsuit. During the trial, although the defendant did not admit the authenticity of the invoice submitted by the plaintiff for the purchase of the allegedly infringing goods in Kunming, the defendant admitted that the physical allegedly infringing goods were produced by the defendant and that they were sold in Kunming.

It was also found that the defendant, Xiaguan Tuocha Company, is a non-listed joint-stock company established on March 14, 1995, primarily engaged in the production and sale of tea. The plaintiff, Cao Xiaodong, is the legal representative of Yunnan Jin Ge Tie Ma Tea Industry Co., Ltd., which was established on February 6, 2007, and is mainly engaged in the sale of tea, agricultural and sideline products, etc. On August 16, 2009, Cao Xiaodong signed a "Trademark License Contract" with Yunnan Jin Ge Tie Ma Tea Industry Co., Ltd., agreeing to license the use of Registered Trademark No. 5492697 on tea products, with the license term from June 14, 2009, to June 14, 2019. Yunnan Jin Ge Tie Ma Tea Industry Co., Ltd. used the registered trademark "Jin Ge Tie Ma" No. 5492697 on various products such as Jingmai Ancient Tree Tea and Jingmai Tuocha. On March 13, 2015, a third party, Han Yongguo, applied to the Trademark Office of the State Administration for Industry and Commerce to cancel Cao Xiaodong's registration of Trademark No. 5492697 in Class 30 "Jin Ge Tie Ma." Subsequently, the Trademark Office determined that the grounds for cancellation raised by Han Yongguo were untenable and, on December 4, 2015, decided to reject Han Yongguo's cancellation application.

The court of first instance held that the issues in dispute were: 1. Whether the allegedly infringing goods infringed Cao Xiaodong's exclusive right to use the trademark in question; 2. If infringement was established, how should the defendant bear legal liability. Article 57 of the Trademark Law of the People's Republic of China (hereinafter "Trademark Law") provides that any of the following acts shall constitute an infringement of the exclusive right to use a registered trademark: (1) using a trademark identical to the registered trademark on the same goods without the permission of the trademark registrant; (2) using a trademark similar to the registered trademark on the same goods, or using a trademark identical or similar to the registered trademark on similar goods, without the permission of the trademark registrant, where such use is likely to cause confusion. In this case, the plaintiff claimed that the defendant used a trademark identical to its registered trademark on the same goods. The defendant argued that "Jia Wu Jin Ge Tie Ma Tie Bing" was merely the name of a series of products produced by the defendant and was not used as a trademark. Regarding whether the defendant's use of the mark "Jia Wu Jin Ge Tie Ma Tie Bing" constituted trademark use, the court of first instance held that, according to Article 48 of the Trademark Law, the use of a trademark refers to the act of using the trademark on goods, goods packaging or containers, and transaction documents, or using the trademark in advertising, exhibitions, and other commercial activities, for the purpose of identifying the source of the goods. Therefore, distinctiveness is a basic characteristic of a trademark. In this case, the defendant's use of the mark "Jia Wu Jin Ge Tie Ma Tie Bing" was on the inner and outer packaging of the allegedly infringing goods, accompanied by a pattern of a horse in a galloping posture. Additionally, the registered trademark "Song He Yan Nian" and the characters "Xiaguan Tuocha" were marked on both the inner and outer packaging of the allegedly infringing goods. Therefore, the defendant's use was merely as a decoration of the goods, not as a trademark use. According to Article 76 of the Implementing Regulations of the Trademark Law of the People's Republic of China, using a mark identical or similar to another person's registered trademark as the name or decoration of goods on the same or similar goods, thereby misleading the public, constitutes an act infringing the exclusive right to use a registered trademark as provided in Article 57, Item (2) of the Trademark Law. Upon examination, the designated goods for the plaintiff's Registered Trademark No. 5492697 are in Class 30, including tea, honey, sugar, coffee, etc., while the allegedly infringing goods are tea, which are the same type of goods as those designated for the plaintiff's registered trademark. At the same time, comparing the visual effects of the mark used by the defendant with the plaintiff's registered trademark: In terms of the constituent elements of the trademark, the plaintiff's registered trademark is a combined mark of text and graphics. The text "Jin Ge Tie Ma" is in horizontal traditional Chinese characters, with a leaf pattern below the text. In contrast, the characters "Jin Ge Tie Ma" used by the defendant are in simplified Chinese characters and do not include the leaf pattern. Therefore, the plaintiff's registered trademark and the mark used by the defendant are not identical. However, there are some similar elements in their composition. Although the defendant claimed that it used the mark "Jia Wu Jin Ge Tie Ma Tie Bing" as a whole, upon examination, the characters "Jia Wu" and "Tie Bing" are smaller in font, while the four characters "Jin Ge Tie Ma" are larger in font and located in conspicuous positions on both the outer and inner packaging of the tea cakes. Although the plaintiff's trademark is a combined mark of text and graphics, the text "Jin Ge Tie Ma" is more prominent among the constituent elements of the plaintiff's registered trademark. The defendant prominently used the four characters "Jin Ge Tie Ma," and although the font is different, the pronunciation and meaning are the same. Therefore, the two are similar.

However, the existence of similar elements in visual effect does not necessarily lead to a finding of infringement. According to Article 76 of the Implementing Regulations of the Trademark Law, using a mark similar to another person's registered trademark as a decoration of goods on the same goods, thereby misleading the public, constitutes an act infringing the exclusive right to use a registered trademark. At the same time, this court held that when determining whether it is likely to cause confusion or mislead the public, in addition to considering the factor of similarity, it should also comprehensively consider factors such as the actual use of the trademark for which protection is claimed and the allegedly infringing mark, the history of use, and the perception of the relevant public. In this case, first, the plaintiff had registered the "Jin Ge Tie Ma" trademark No. 5492697 as early as June 14, 2009, while the defendant's "Song He Yan Nian" and "Xiaguan Tuocha" trademarks were registered in 2010 and 2014 respectively, both later than the plaintiff's trademark registration. Second, the plaintiff licensed Yunnan Jin Ge Tie Ma Tea Industry Co., Ltd. to use its registered trademark on August 16, 2009, while the defendant produced the allegedly infringing goods in 2014, also later than the time when the plaintiff's registered trademark was used. Third, Yunnan Jin Ge Tie Ma Tea Industry Co., Ltd. used the registered trademark "Jin Ge Tie Ma" No. 5492697 on multiple tea products, has formed a certain market share, and has a certain consumer base. The defendant's prominent use of the "Jin Ge Tie Ma" mark on the allegedly infringing goods is likely to cause confusion and mislead the relevant public. In summary, the defendant used a mark similar to the plaintiff's registered trademark in question as a decoration of goods on the same goods, misleading the public, and such use was without the plaintiff's permission. Therefore, it infringed the plaintiff's exclusive right to use the registered trademark "Jin Ge Tie Ma" No. 5492697.

Regarding how the defendant should bear legal liability, according to the first paragraph of Article 21 of the Interpretation of the Supreme People's Court on the Application of Law in the Trial of Civil Disputes over Trademark Cases, if infringement is established, the court may order the cessation of infringement, compensation for losses, elimination of adverse effects, and other civil liabilities. In this case, the plaintiff claimed that the defendant engaged in production and sales. However, during the trial, the plaintiff explicitly only sought cessation of sales. This claim is in accordance with the law and should be supported. Regarding the plaintiff's request for the defendant to publish a statement of apology in provincial media to eliminate adverse effects, because the act of trademark infringement primarily infringes property rights, and the defendant produced these products only in 2014 and has since ceased production, the scope of impact is extremely limited. This court holds that ordering the cessation of sales is sufficient to stop the adverse effects. Therefore, this request is not supported. Regarding the claim for compensation for losses, the defendant argued that since the plaintiff had not used its registered trademark for many years, even if infringement was established, the defendant should not bear liability for damages. In this regard, the court of first instance held that the plaintiff submitted a "Trademark License Contract" and related tea products, which could prove that the plaintiff licensed others to use its registered trademark. Therefore, the defendant's defense cannot stand. The plaintiff claimed compensation for losses of RMB 1,260,000 in this case. The plaintiff argued that the defendant issued 252,000 cakes of the allegedly infringing goods, calculated at a profit of RMB 5 per cake, totaling RMB 1,260,000. However, this claim lacks factual basis and is not accepted by this court. According to Paragraph 3 of Article 63 of the Trademark Law, if the actual losses suffered by the right holder due to infringement, the profits gained by the infringer due to infringement, and the license fees for the registered trademark are difficult to determine, the People's Court shall, based on the circumstances of the infringement, grant compensation of up to RMB 3 million. In this case, the plaintiff failed to submit evidence proving its actual losses or the illegal gains of the infringer, and the trademark license fees could not be determined. Taking into account factors such as the degree of fame of the trademark in question, the nature and duration of the defendant's infringement, the scale of the defendant's business, and the reasonable expenses paid by the plaintiff for enforcing its rights, the court discretionarily orders the defendant to compensate the plaintiff for economic losses totaling RMB 200,000. Regarding the plaintiff's request for compensation of attorney's fees and other reasonable expenses of RMB 63,990, as this has already been considered in determining the compensation for economic losses, this request is not supported.

The court of first instance ruled: 1. Yunnan Xiaguan Tuocha (Group) Co., Ltd. shall immediately cease the sale of infringing goods bearing the "Jin Ge Tie Ma" mark; 2. Yunnan Xiaguan Tuocha (Group) Co., Ltd. shall compensate Cao Xiaodong for economic losses of RMB 200,000 within ten days after the judgment takes effect; 3. Cao Xiaodong's other claims are dismissed.

Xiaguan Tuocha Company, dissatisfied with the first-instance judgment, filed an appeal to the Yunnan High People's Court, requesting: reversal of the first-instance judgment. The facts and reasons for its appeal were as follows: 1. Cao Xiaodong believed that Xiaguan Tuocha Company infringed his rights by using an identical mark to Cao Xiaodong's Trademark No. 5492697 "Jinge Tima" on the packaging of its "Jiawu Jinge Tima Tiebing" product produced in 2014, but the first-instance court found only similarity rather than identity, and on that basis found infringement. This violated the principle of "no trial without complaint" in Chinese civil adjudication. 2. Xiaguan Tuocha Company prominently marked its own registered trademark and manufacturer name in a conspicuous place and bright colors on its "Jiawu Jinge Tima Tiebing" product, and that trademark itself was a well-known trademark. Cao Xiaodong's trademark lacked distinctiveness and recognition. The relevant public would not confuse the source of the company's "Jiawu Jinge Tima Tiebing" product with the source of the product identified by Cao Xiaodong's registered trademark, nor would it mislead the public. According to relevant provisions of Chinese trademark law, Xiaguan Tuocha Company's "Jiawu Jinge Tima Tiebing" product did not infringe Cao Xiaodong's rights. 3. Even if Xiaguan Tuocha Company constituted infringement, Cao Xiaodong had no evidence to prove that he had produced or sold goods identified by his registered trademark within three years prior to filing the lawsuit. According to relevant provisions of trademark law, Xiaguan Tuocha Company was not required to compensate Cao Xiaodong for economic losses.

Facts found by the court of second instance: During the second instance, Xiaguan Tuocha Company submitted a copy of the "Notice of Acceptance of Application for Revocation of a Registered Trademark for Non-Use for Three Consecutive Years" issued by the Trademark Office on April 11, 2016, seeking to prove that the trademark in question had not been used for three years prior to the lawsuit. Upon cross-examination, Cao Xiaodong confirmed that the copy was consistent with the original and recognized its authenticity and legality, but argued it could not prove Xiaguan Tuocha Company's point, because the notice only proved that Xiaguan Tuocha Company's application was accepted, but the Trademark Office had not yet made a finding on whether Cao Xiaodong's trademark had not been used for three consecutive years. The court of second instance, upon review, held that this notice indeed only proved that Xiaguan Tuocha Company's application was accepted, and its ground for revocation based on "non-use for three consecutive years" had not yet been confirmed by the Trademark Office. Accordingly, the court did not recognize the probative value of this notice. Regarding the facts found by the first-instance judgment, except that Xiaguan Tuocha Company insisted that the trademark in question had not been used for three consecutive years prior to Cao Xiaodong's filing of this lawsuit, the parties had no objection to the other facts found by the first-instance judgment, which the court of second instance confirmed. Regarding whether the trademark in question had been unused for three consecutive years, the court of second instance, upon review, held that the "Decision on the Application for Revocation of Registered Trademark No. 5492697, Class 30 'Jinge Tima' for Non-Use for Three Consecutive Years" issued by the Trademark Office on December 4, 2015, which Cao Xiaodong submitted to the first-instance court, could prove that on March 13, 2015, a third party, Han Yongguo, had applied to the Trademark Office for revocation on the ground that Cao Xiaodong's trademark in question had not been used for three consecutive years. The Trademark Office, upon review, held that the evidence of use submitted by Cao Xiaodong was valid and could prove that the trademark in question was used during the period from March 13, 2012 to March 12, 2015, and that Han Yongguo's ground for non-use for three consecutive years was untenable, and accordingly rejected Han Yongguo's revocation application. The court of second instance held that the above finding by the Trademark Office had already proved that the trademark in question was used during the period from March 13, 2012 to March 12, 2015, and Xiaguan Tuocha Company's defense that the trademark in question had not been used for three years prior to the filing of this lawsuit, i.e., from February 23, 2013 to February 22, 2016, was not established.

The court of second instance held that, upon trial, the issues in dispute in this case were as follows:

I. Whether the first-instance judgment violated the principle of "no trial without complaint"? The court of second instance held that the legal principle of "no trial without complaint" in civil litigation mainly means that the court can only hear and decide on the claims raised by the parties, and cannot exceed the scope of the parties' claims to hear and decide on claims not raised by the parties. Therefore, "no trial without complaint" refers to the parties' claims, not to the facts and reasons on which the claims are based. In this case, Cao Xiaodong, as the owner of the right to the trademark in question "Jinge Tima", filed an infringement lawsuit on the ground that Xiaguan Tuocha Company's relevant conduct infringed this trademark, and raised related claims for infringement liability. The first-instance court, based on the specific circumstances of this case and relevant legal provisions, found Xiaguan Tuocha Company infringed Cao Xiaodong's rights on grounds different from those alleged by Cao Xiaodong, i.e., it found that the mark used in the packaging and decoration of Xiaguan Tuocha Company's accused infringing goods was "similar" to Cao Xiaodong's registered trademark "Jinge Tima", rather than "identical" as claimed by Cao Xiaodong, and thereby found infringement. This finding did not exceed the claims raised by Cao Xiaodong based on the infringement accusation. Accordingly, the court of second instance held that the first-instance judgment did not violate the principle of "no trial without complaint".

II. Whether Xiaguan Tuocha Company's conduct infringed Cao Xiaodong's exclusive right to use the registered trademark "Jinge Tima"? The first-instance court found that the "Jinge Tima" mark used in the packaging and decoration of Xiaguan Tuocha Company's accused infringing goods was similar to Cao Xiaodong's trademark "Jinge Tima", and that this similarity was likely to cause the relevant public to confuse the accused infringing goods with Cao Xiaodong's trademark, misleading the public. Therefore, pursuant to Article 76 of the Implementing Regulations of the Trademark Law, it found Xiaguan Tuocha Company infringed. However, Xiaguan Tuocha Company argued that the "Jinge Tima" mark used in the packaging and decoration of the accused infringing goods was neither identical nor similar to the trademark "Jinge Tima", and would not mislead the public, and therefore did not constitute infringement.

The court of second instance held that, in trademark infringement cases, how to determine whether a trademark or mark used on accused infringing goods is similar to the right holder's registered trademark is clearly provided in Article 9(2) and Article 10 of the Judicial Interpretation of the Trademark Law. Article 9(2) of that interpretation provides: "Similar trademarks as referred to in Article 52(1) of the Trademark Law mean that the trademark accused of infringement, when compared with the plaintiff's registered trademark, is similar in the shape, pronunciation, or meaning of the characters, or in the composition, color, or overall structure of the design, or in the three-dimensional shape or color combination, and is likely to cause the relevant public to mistake the source of the goods or to believe that the source of the accused goods has a specific connection with the source of the goods of the plaintiff's registered trademark." As for the principles of comparison, Article 10 of the interpretation provides: "When determining whether trademarks are identical or similar pursuant to Article 52(1) of the Trademark Law, the People's Court shall follow the following principles: (1) using the general attention of the relevant public as the standard; (2) conducting both an overall comparison of the trademarks and a comparison of the main parts of the trademarks, and the comparison shall be conducted separately under the condition of isolation; (3) when determining whether trademarks are similar, the distinctiveness and recognition of the registered trademark requesting protection shall be considered." Specifically in this case, first, comparing the "Jinge Tima" mark used in the packaging and decoration of the accused infringing goods with the trademark in question "Jinge Tima", there was no difference in pronunciation or meaning, but there were the following differences in visual effect: 1. In terms of arrangement, the four characters "Jinge Tima" of the former were arranged vertically, while this court, after reviewing the physical pictures of Cao Xiaodong's products submitted to the court, found that the four characters "Jinge Tima" in the trademark in question were essentially arranged horizontally; 2. In terms of composition, the main image of the former was the four vertical characters "Jinge Tima" next to a galloping horse, while the latter had a leaf pattern below the four horizontal characters "Jinge Tima"; 3. In terms of font and script, the former was in simplified Chinese, while the latter was in traditional Chinese, and the shapes of the characters were also distinctly different. This court held that, based on the above comparison results, although the two were identical in pronunciation and meaning, because the trademark in question was a combined trademark of characters and graphics, and was printed on the packaging of goods, for the relevant public, the differences in visual effect had a greater impact. In other words, the court of second instance held that the above differences in visual effect between the two could offset any confusion or misleading of the public that might be caused by the identity in pronunciation and meaning. Second, from the overall packaging and decoration of the accused infringing goods, although the four characters "Jinge Tima" on the packaging were enlarged and prominent, and relatively conspicuous in the decoration, this mark was only used on the front of the packaging. The sides and back of the outer packaging clearly indicated Xiaguan Tuocha Company's company name and address, and the upper left corner of the front prominently displayed Xiaguan Tuocha Company's own "Xiaguan Tuocha" trademark in red. Therefore, overall, the relevant public would not mistake the accused infringing goods for the goods of the trademark in question or believe they had a specific connection with those goods. Third, from the perspective of trademark recognition and distinctiveness, a certificate of "China Time-honored Brand" submitted by Xiaguan Tuocha Company could prove that the "Xiaguan Tuocha" trademark used on the accused infringing goods had been recognized as a "China Time-honored Brand" by the Ministry of Commerce of the PRC. However, Cao Xiaodong did not submit any evidence showing that, apart from registration, the trademark in question had received any other certification from a national authority indicating its recognition. The court of second instance inferred from this that the recognition of the "Xiaguan Tuocha" trademark used on the accused infringing goods was far higher than that of the trademark in question, and the accused infringing goods had no need to free-ride on the trademark in question to enhance their own recognition. Moreover, the four characters "Jinge Tima" used in the trademark in question often appear in literary works, and even if the relevant public noticed these four characters on the accused infringing goods, they would not necessarily associate the accused infringing goods with the goods of the trademark in question, nor would they inevitably and mistakenly believe that both were goods produced by Cao Xiaodong or a company authorized by Cao Xiaodong.

In view of this, the court of second instance held that the mark used in the packaging and decoration of the accused infringing goods was neither similar nor identical to the trademark in question, and would not mislead the public. Xiaguan Tuocha Company's use of the "Jinge Tima" mark on the packaging and decoration of its "Jinge Tima" series tea cakes did not constitute an infringement of Cao Xiaodong's exclusive right to use the registered trademark as provided in Article 57(2) of the Trademark Law. The first-instance court's finding that the two were similar and would mislead the public, and accordingly finding Xiaguan Tuocha Company infringed, was erroneous and was corrected. Since Xiaguan Tuocha Company did not infringe Cao Xiaodong's rights, Cao Xiaodong's claims for infringement liability against Xiaguan Tuocha Company based on that accusation should also not be supported. Judgment of the second instance: The first-instance judgment was reversed, and all of Cao Xiaodong's claims were dismissed.

This court holds that, based on the facts found by the courts of first and second instance, combined with the parties' reasons for retrial application and defense opinions, the issue in dispute in this case is whether the accused infringing goods infringed Cao Xiaodong's exclusive right to use the trademark in question.

Article 57 of the Trademark Law of the People's Republic of China provides that any of the following acts shall constitute an infringement of the exclusive right to use a registered trademark: (1) using a trademark identical to a registered trademark on the same goods without the permission of the trademark registrant; (2) using a trademark similar to a registered trademark on the same goods, or using a trademark identical or similar to a registered trademark on similar goods, without the permission of the trademark registrant, which is likely to cause confusion. In this case, Cao Xiaodong's registered trademark No. 5492697 is approved for use on goods in Class 30, including tea, honey, sugar, coffee, etc., while the accused infringing goods are tea, which belongs to the same type of goods as those for which Cao Xiaodong's registered trademark is approved. Meanwhile, comparing the mark used by Xiaguan Tuocha Company with Cao Xiaodong's registered trademark in terms of visual effect: from the constituent elements of the trademark, Cao Xiaodong's registered trademark is a combined trademark of characters and graphics, with the characters "Jinge Tima" in traditional Chinese arranged horizontally, and a leaf pattern below the characters "Jinge Tima"; whereas the characters "Jinge Tima" used by Xiaguan Tuocha Company are in simplified Chinese and do not include the leaf pattern. Therefore, Cao Xiaodong's registered trademark and the mark used by Xiaguan Tuocha Company are not identical. However, there are certain similar elements in their constituent parts. Although Xiaguan Tuocha Company argued that it used the "Jiawu Jinge Tima Tiebing" mark as a whole, upon review, the characters "Jiawu" and "Tiebing" are in a smaller font, while the four characters "Jinge Tima" are in a larger font and located in prominent positions on the outer packaging and inner packaging of the tea cake. Although Cao Xiaodong's registered trademark is a combined trademark of characters and graphics, the characters "Jinge Tima" are more prominent among the constituent elements of Cao Xiaodong's registered trademark. Xiaguan Tuocha Company prominently used the four characters "Jinge Tima", and although the fonts are different, the pronunciation and meaning are identical. Therefore, the two are similar, and their use on the same type of tea goods is likely to cause confusion among the relevant public. The finding of the court of second instance that "the mark used in the packaging and decoration of the accused infringing goods was neither similar nor identical to the trademark in question, and would not mislead the public" was erroneous, and this court corrects it.

Furthermore, the court of first instance inferred that "the recognition of the Xiaguan Tuocha trademark used on the accused infringing goods was far higher than that of the trademark in question, and the accused infringing goods had no need to free-ride on the trademark in question to enhance their own recognition." Regarding this inference, this court holds that, first, a trademark, as a sign that distinguishes the source of goods or services, has its basic attribute of being a distinguisher. Although "Jinge Tima" is a common phrase in literary works, its registration for use on goods in Class 30 such as tea, honey, sugar, and coffee has distinctiveness and can serve to identify the source of goods. The right to the registered trademark that Cao Xiaodong enjoys over this mark is not different from that of an ordinary registered trademark simply because the phrase commonly appears in literary works. Second, when a People's Court finds facts, it should do so based on examining and adjudicating the evidence provided by the parties, not by making simple inferences. Even if it is necessary to infer the relevant intent of a party based on the preponderance of evidence in the case, such an inference must be made in conjunction with the facts found based on relevant evidence. According to the facts found by the first-instance court, Cao Xiaodong had already registered the "Jinge Tima" trademark No. 5492697 on June 14, 2009, while Xiaguan Tuocha Company's "Songhe Yannian" trademark (No. 6209882) and "Xiaguan Tuocha" trademark (No. 12201774) were registered in 2010 and 2014 respectively, both later than the registration time of the plaintiff's trademark. Cao Xiaodong licensed Yunnan Jinge Tima Tea Industry Co., Ltd. to use his registered trademark on August 16, 2009, while Xiaguan Tuocha Company produced the accused infringing goods in 2014, also later than the time when Cao Xiaodong's registered trademark began to be used. Yunnan Jinge Tima Tea Industry Co., Ltd. used the "Jinge Tima" registered trademark No. 5492697 on multiple types of tea products, and had formed a certain market share with a certain consumer base. In the absence of evidence proving that the "Xiaguan Tuocha" trademark (No. 12201774) had higher recognition, the inference made by the court of first instance had no factual basis. Finally, even if the Xiaguan Tuocha trademark had higher recognition than the trademark in dispute in this case, although the finding of the court of first instance that the accused infringing goods had no need to free-ride on the trademark in question to enhance their own recognition had a certain possibility, this inference ignored the functions and effects of a registered trademark as a distinctive civil right. It not only has the right to prohibit others from using the registered trademark on identical or similar goods, but also has the right to use its registered trademark to identify its goods or services and to establish a connection between that trademark and the source of its goods in the minds of the relevant public. Whether the relevant public will be confused or misled includes not only mistaking goods using the accused infringing mark for the trademark owner's goods or believing they have some connection with the trademark owner, but also mistaking the trademark owner's goods for the accused infringer's goods or believing that the trademark owner has some connection with the accused infringer, thereby hindering the trademark owner from exercising its exclusive right to use the registered trademark and substantively hindering the registered trademark from playing its role of distinguishing the source. Therefore, if the court were to hold that a party with a more well-known registered trademark can arbitrarily use another person's registered trademark on its goods, this would substantially damage the basic function of that registered trademark in distinguishing the source of goods, causing fundamental damage to the exclusive right to use that registered trademark. The court of second instance found that the accused infringing goods did not constitute infringement of the exclusive right to use the registered trademark in question on the ground that the accused infringing goods' own trademark had high recognition. This finding was erroneous in both fact and law, and this court corrects it.

In summary, Xiaguan Tuocha Company, without permission, used a mark similar to Cao Xiaodong's registered trademark in question on the same type of goods, which is likely to cause confusion among the relevant public, and infringed Cao Xiaodong's exclusive right to use the registered trademark "Jinge Tima" No. 5492697. The finding of the second-instance judgment that the accused conduct did not constitute an infringement of Cao Xiaodong's exclusive right to use the registered trademark under Article 57(2) of the Trademark Law was erroneous in both fact and law, and this court hereby reverses it. The finding of the first-instance judgment that Xiaguan Tuocha Company, without Cao Xiaodong's permission, used a mark similar to Cao Xiaodong's trademark in question as a decoration on the same type of goods, misleading the public, and that this conduct infringed Cao Xiaodong's exclusive right to use the trademark in question, was clear in fact and correct in law, and this court affirms it.

This court holds that Cao Xiaodong's application for retrial meets the circumstances provided in Article 200 of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China and should be granted. Pursuant to Article 207(1) and Article 170(1)(2) of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China, the judgment is as follows:

1. The civil judgment (2016) Yun Min Zhong No. 738 of the Yunnan High People's Court is reversed;

2. The civil judgment (2016) Yun 01 Min Chu No. 246 of the Kunming Intermediate People's Court of Yunnan Province is affirmed.

The first-instance case acceptance fee of RMB 16,715.91 and the second-instance case acceptance fee of RMB 4,300, totaling RMB 21,015.91, shall be borne by Yunnan Xiaguan Tuocha (Group) Co., Ltd.

This judgment is final.
